newsitem.title: UK: Sears down as Freemans sale hits snag.
newsitem.headline: Sears down as Freemans sale hits snag.

text.p: Shares in Sears Plc dropped on Friday after privately-owned retail group Littlewoods said it had withdrawn from talks to buy Sears' Freemans catalogue unit.
Sears shares were down 2-1/2p at 79-1/2 by 1320 GMT, after being unchanged shortly before the Littlewoods move was announced.
Last month Sears said its was pressing on the with the sale Commission (MMC) investigation into the proposed deal.
Yet Littlewoods said on Friday it had pulled out of the talks, adding that it had become clear that Sears was in talks to sell the unit to unnamed other parties.
Analysts said the failure of the disposal was no great surprise given the fact that the MMC was investigating.
"If there was a risk that the MMC might block the deal Sears was duty bound to try to find an alternative," said David Stoddart, analyst at Henderson Crosthwaite.
"If there was a spanner thrown into the works it was when the deal was referred to the MMC."

The disposal to Littlewoods was part of continuing restructuring measures by chief executive Liam Strong, under pressure to revitalise the group because of the underperformance of its shares since he took control five years ago.
The 395 million stg sale of the Freemans arm underpinned a pledge to return some 410 million in cash to shareholders.
